notes: THE SUBJECT, AND IT TOOK TWO ROUNDS AND TWO AGENTS. Kevin Johnson '89: 20.4 points, 12.2 assists, 39.2 minutes, usg 21.2, TS .597, BPM 4.2, All-NBA 2nd. recal_174 declined him from the attribute side, proved the `volume` bar is a usage RATE and his is the 50th percentile of 1989, and named the door here: 'the subject's passer credit is 5.30 against Stockton '90's 13.38 because his efficiency factor is 0.72 against 1.00'. This round opened that door and the one beside it. His passer term goes 5.295 -> 13.19: gate 0.328 -> 0.530 and eff factor 0.725 -> 1.000. off 75 -> 81, ovr 69 -> 74.

WHY BOTH GATES AND NOT ONE, MEASURED FIRST AND DECLINED IN PUBLIC. The efficiency factor alone reaches OFF 77 and NOT ONE POINT MORE — _ge is a multiplier clamped at 1.0, so the most it can add the subject is 2.01 of o_score, and setting it to 1.0 for the whole class (which fails three Mark Jackson pins) still prints him 77. That was this round's first report and Tomer's answer was 'land 77 ... if we can increase nash stockton and kevin johnson without billups tho, that will be fine'. The band top is what carries the last four points, and it is measured rather than fitted: it is the only knob that moves the subject without touching Billups, whose volume 66 sits so far inside the band that his gate changes by a twentieth.

WHY 93 AND NOT A NUMBER INSIDE THE WINDOW. The feasible window under his wall is PD_V_HI 91 to 94 — the subject reads 81 across all four and Billups reads 92 across all four — so a fitted midpoint was available and was NOT used. 93.0 is the measured p90 of volume among the 1,486 cards that clear the term's own playvol foot, it lands inside the window, and the dispatch's rule is to prefer the measured value where one does. Sweep, all with the efficiency re-cut in place: 68 subject 77 Billups 91; 85-88 subject 80 Billups 91; 89-90 subject 80 Billups 92; 91-94 subject 81 Billups 92; 95 subject 81 BILLUPS 93, the reading he refused.

THE FOOTPRINT. 694 cards move on OFF — 585 up, 109 down, largest rise +7 (Scott Skiles '93 63 -> 70), largest fall -2. 516 move on OVR, max 5. ZERO move on DEF. Every mover clears playvol 70; no card outside the distributor class is touched, which is why Josh Hart '25, Cedric Maxwell '80, Kyle Korver '15, Richaun Holmes '21, Andre Drummond '20 and the whole low-usage family round 174 could not avoid breaking are byte-identical here. ANCHORS: 177 pins, 0 failing, mean |error| 0.80 against main's 0.85 — the board is closer to his rulings after this round than before it, on the same measure.

WHAT THE CLASS LOOKS LIKE NOW. The efficiency factor pays the class's median passer 0.50 and its p90 1.00, against a ramp that used to pay 85% of the class the floor. The volume gate pays a distributor in full at volume 10 and nothing at 93, against a gate that used to pay nothing from 68 — the 60th percentile of the class it ranks. Both constants are the class's own quantiles, which is the construction recal_130 settled ('the class's own upper quartile, MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN') and recal_117 used on the playvol ramp of this same term; the one gate r117 left fitted and the one factor it left uncut are the two this round closes.

THIRTY-EIGHT FULL-BOARD MEASUREMENTS stand behind these two numbers: the base reproducing all 10,000 cards byte-for-byte, the efficiency factor's arithmetic ceiling, six class-derived cuts of that ramp, fourteen sizes of the term, and seventeen feet and tops of the volume band — each graded by data/anchors.py itself on a written-out board, never by hand.
